title: 非正弦电压的有效值、平均值与仪表读数
statement: 求 v 的有效值 V 和平均值，以及电阻吸收的平均功率 P。再判断两种电压表的读数。

questions.explain: 正弦量在一个周期内的平均值为零，所以平均值就是直流分量 10 V。

questions.ask: 电阻吸收的平均功率 P = ?
用磁电系（永磁动圈式）电压表测 v，读数约为多少？
choiceExplain: 有效值由电磁系或电动系电压表测量。
100 V 只是基波有效值；磁电系仪表对正弦分量的平均偏转为零。
141.4 V 是基波的振幅，磁电系仪表对正弦分量的平均偏转为零。
questions.explain: 磁电系仪表的偏转与电流的平均值成正比，读数是**直流分量**（平均值）10 V。

questions.ask: 用电磁系（动铁式）电压表测 v，读数约为多少？
choiceExplain: 电磁系仪表的转矩与 i² 成正比，读的是有效值，不是平均值。
140 V 是把三个有效值直接相加——有效值不能相加。
questions.explain: 电磁系仪表读**有效值**：104.9 V。

hints: 非正弦周期量的有效值不是各次谐波有效值之和，而是“平方和再开方”。
先把每一项换成有效值：直流 10 V，基波 100√2/√2 = 100 V，3 次谐波 30 V。初相与有效值无关。
平均功率可以用 V²/R，也可以把各次谐波的功率相加。磁电系仪表读平均值，电磁系读有效值。
solution: **3. 平均值。** 正弦分量在一个周期内平均为零，V_0 = **10 V**。
**5. 仪表。** 磁电系仪表反映平均值，读 **10 V**；电磁系（以及电动系）仪表反映有效值，读 **104.9 V**。

en.title: rms value, average value and meter readings of a non-sinusoidal voltage
statement: The voltage across a resistor R = 50 Ω is v = 10 + 100√2 cos(314t) + 30√2 cos(942t − 60°) V.
Find the rms value V and the average value of v, and the average power P absorbed by the resistor. Then decide what two kinds of voltmeter read.
hints: The rms value of a non-sinusoidal periodic quantity is not the sum of the harmonics' rms values but the square root of the sum of their squares.
Turn every term into an rms value first: DC 10 V, fundamental 100√2/√2 = 100 V, 3rd harmonic 30 V. The initial phases do not matter for rms values.
The average power is V²/R, or the sum of the harmonics' powers. A moving-coil meter reads the average value, a moving-iron meter the rms value.
solution: **1. rms value of each component.** DC V_0 = 10 V; fundamental V_1 = 100√2/√2 = 100 V; 3rd harmonic (942 = 3 × 314) V_3 = 30 V. The −60° phase does not affect the rms value.
**3. Average value.** The sinusoidal terms average to zero over a period, V_0 = **10 V**.
**Check:** harmonic by harmonic, P_0 = 10²/50 = 2 W, P_1 = 100²/50 = 200 W, P_3 = 30²/50 = 18 W, total 220 W — the same.
**5. Meters.** A moving-coil meter responds to the average value and reads **10 V**; a moving-iron (or electrodynamic) meter responds to the rms value and reads **104.9 V**.

questions.explain: V = √(V_0² + V_1² + V_3²) = √(10² + 100² + 30²) = √11000 ≈ 104.9 V. Use the **rms value** of each harmonic (100√2 peak is 100 V rms).
A sinusoid averages to zero over a period, so the average value is the DC component, 10 V.

questions.ask: Average power absorbed by the resistor, P = ?
questions.explain: For a resistor P = V²/R = 11000/50 = 220 W; it also equals the sum of the harmonic powers 10²/50 + 100²/50 + 30²/50 = 2 + 200 + 18 = 220 W.

questions.ask: What does a moving-coil (permanent-magnet) voltmeter read when measuring v?
choiceExplain: The rms value is what a moving-iron or electrodynamic voltmeter reads.
100 V is only the rms value of the fundamental; a moving-coil meter averages every sinusoidal component to zero.
141.4 V is the amplitude of the fundamental; a moving-coil meter averages every sinusoidal component to zero.
questions.explain: A moving-coil meter deflects in proportion to the average current, so it reads the **DC component** (average value), 10 V.

questions.ask: What does a moving-iron voltmeter read when measuring v?
choiceExplain: A moving-iron meter's torque is proportional to i², so it reads the rms value, not the average.
140 V adds the three rms values directly — rms values do not add.
That uses the amplitudes 100√2 V and 30√2 V as if they were rms values: √(10² + 141.4² + 42.43²) = 148.0 V.
questions.explain: A moving-iron meter reads the **rms value**: 104.9 V.
